'''William Schmidt''' was a Decipher-era [[Squadron Members|Squadron Member]], Gold 18 from Tempe, AZ, whose slot was marked Retired after Decipher's SWCCG run.<ref name="sm-fan" />

He learned the game in early 1996 at the Bookstar in Tempe. Kendrick Summers recruited him after the 1996 Rebel Leader Tour stop there. The [[1997 Tatooine Regionals (Phoenix)]] he hosted drew 36 players and was won by [[Jeremy LaMere]] over Brandon Allen.<ref name="decsq-prof" />

He wrote three strategy articles for [[Scrye]], beta-tested Decipher's tournament program and wrote a card-management program, the Card Organizer. Just under 200 different players had attended his tournaments by then.<ref name="decsq-prof" />

== In their own words ==

<blockquote>
Introduction

          I consider myself a veteran of
the Star Wars: CCG and was first introduced to it very early in
1996 by Jason Meyer, my assistant manager at the Bookstar where I
worked. I first purchased a starter deck and a couple of boosters
(which I begged my wife for) and from there I later bought a box
of Premiere boosters and then another. It's great to know you
have a loving wife who supports your habit even when she doesn't
fully understand it.

          Afterward, Jason taught me how
to play and I look fondly on those days where a game could last
for nearly three hours (2 hours 45 minutes is our record)! We
made a lot of mistakes back then. He and I played with a couple
others every Sunday evening at Bookstar, a Gaming Event that
still continues. I discovered Decipher's player list and e-mailed
everyone in our area. Our numbers at Bookstar grew and many of
today's regular players were part of that first e-mail. Things
were going well and players were eager to test themselves so I
decided to apply as a Director.

1996

          Star Wars: CCG really exploded
here in the desert when I read about the Rebel Leader Tour in the
summer of 1996. I sent an e-mail to Sandy Wible (Rebel Base
Leader at the time) and he forwarded it to Kendrick Summers (Gold
Leader, now Marketing Manager). Kendrick called me the next day.
After all arrangements were made, when he arrived he was greeted
by a huge Bookstar crowd of Star Wars fans. It was after this
event that Kendrick offered me a position with Gold Squadron,
which I eagerly accepted.

1997

          The next year, 1997, I held my
first Regional Qualifier at a local convention. Kendrick
participated with this and though I was disappointed at only
having 36 players show he assured me that this was not a bad
number to draw. If only the players knew they did not have to pay
the convention price to play. Oh well. We had a great match
between Jeremy LaMere and Brandon Allen in the final game. As
many of us know know, Jeremy won his second trip to Worlds.

1998

          Early the next year, I was
honored to hold a Pre-release tournament for the Official
Tournament Sealed Deck product. And though I was worried that we
would not get enough product for the potential draw, everything
worked out fine. We had 37 players show up at the Bookstar, which
filled us up to capacity. It was a great turnout and I was
pleased that I beat my record set at 1998's Regionals. Josh
Martin won that tournament.

          Later that year I held my
second Regional Qualifier at Arizona State University. This time
I drew 45 players and though I had to charge for my first
tournament (I dislike charging for tournaments but we had to rent
the room) I was pleased with the turnout. We had a tense final
round between our area big players here for the Qualifier,
Michael Girard and Mike Strahan. Mike Girard of course won that
battle, his first trip to Worlds. Jeremy LaMere had won earlier
in the season.

1999

          Starting this year, I began
writing strategy articles for Star Wars: CCG. So far I have
written three articles for Scrye magazine and though I have not
written for the magazine lately I do plan to continue that again
in the future. Besides, I have not had time to do any writing. I
continuously work on numerous projects for Star Wars (as my wife
can attest). My first was a tournament program I designed in
Microsoft Access. I used that program until Decipher's tournament
program was officially released (which I was happy to Beta Test).

          My current project, however,
is the Card Organizer. For those
familiar with DeckMaker will understand
the concept behind this program. For those not familiar with this
type of program, typical Card Management programs assist you in
maintaining your inventory, trade lists, and deck ideas. The Card
Organizer does more than previous Card Managment
programs because it allows you to do keyword seaches in the
cards. Very helpful. If you are interested in learning more about
the program, click here
and take a look. Let me know what you think.

          Early in 1999 I was offered to
become one of Decipher's Flight Leaders, a special program where
a Squadron Member specializes in doing demonstrations and
conventions. Basically, we meet the players and promote the games
as much as possible. As part of those new duties I held three
demos and the Barnes & Noble stores in Phoenix. Though we did
not have that many participants (LucasFilm did not allow the
stores to advertise) my wife and I had a great time doing demos
with all the younger players.

Other Interests

          My other interests include
reading and writing Science-fiction and fantasy. I have finished
my first fantasy novel and occasionally work on its sequels.
Though I have yet to be published (other than in Scrye), this is
a goal of mine I hope to attain soon. Someday I hope to have my
novels published.

Conclusion

          Currently, I continue with the
Classic Star Wars: CCG but also do a lot of work with the Young
Jedi: CCG. This game is still in its infancy but I expect great
things for it. Since I've started in the games, I have had just
shy of 200 different players attend my numerous Tournaments. I'm
happy to have two Gaming Events started in my area, three
locations where Tournaments are held, and many Directors who
support me and assist in tournaments when necessary. And now that
I have another Squadron Member in the area, Michael Girard, Gold
120, things are expected to get better than ever.

          I am happy to say that Star
Wars: CCG is alive and well here in the deserts of Tatooine. In
1997 we had one person go to Worlds and in 1998 we had two. I'm
proud to be in the Region where we have a three-timer (Jeremy
LaMere) and a first-timer (Michael Girard). We hope to bring more
in the future.

          Here's to the future of Star
Wars and Young Jedi. It is strong here and can only get stronger.
I thank Decipher for the opportunity I have been given to serve
the players here and look forward to what the future will hold.
Come visit me sometime at the Tatooine
Regional Home Page.<ref name="decsq-prof" />
</blockquote>
